subject: EdgeFin performance checkpoints — p95/p99 qualification plan (hosted vs incumbent)
summary: Post-demo follow-up with technical checkpoints to qualify p95/p99 end-to-end latency for hosted Redwood API vs EdgeFin's incumbent provider. Includes explicit load profile, streaming concurrency asks, KV/prefix cache assumptions, and next-step owners for test execution.
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@edgefin.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin — post-demo performance checkpoints (p95/p99)

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the level of detail your SREs shared. Per our conversation, I put together a concise set of technical checkpoints so we can qualify p95/p99 end-to-end latency for Redwood's hosted API versus your current provider. Please find the test-plan attachment (edgefin_p95_test_plan_v1.xlsx) and a short action list below.

High-level asks we discussed:
- Primary SLOs: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms (end-to-end, client-observed)
- Target traffic profile: 75% short requests (~8 tokens avg), 25% long sequences (>=256 tokens)
- Streaming mode: 1–3 concurrent streams per client connection, expect ~60% of requests to use streaming in production
- Concurrency: steady-state 120 RPS with 2-minute bursts to 420 RPS during spikes
- Warmup: include 10–15 minute warm-up window for KV cache + model hot paths

Key technical clarifications we need from EdgeFin to finalize the plan:
1) Representative production traces (sample_production_trace_YYYYMM.zip) showing per-request token counts, observed per-request latencies, and prefix cache hit rates (if available).
2) Expected TLS/session behavior — do you reuse connections or open fresh TLS connections per request?
3) Which percent of requests include short context-only prompts vs. long-context retrieval + generation flows?
4) Any incumbent-specific routing (multi-region fanout) we should mirror in hosted tests?

Proposed measurement methodology (high-level):
- Client-observed end-to-end: measure from client HTTP request start to final byte received (include TLS handshake if not reused).
- Percentile windowing: compute p95/p99 over 5-minute sliding windows, report 95th and 99th across sustained test windows.
- Streaming accounting: measure token-first-byte latency and final-byte latency; report both.

Next steps / owners:
- Asha / EdgeFin: share a 24–48 hour sample trace + confirm TLS behavior (due: Tue 2027-04-12)
- Redwood (Priyom): upload test harness and rough load script, coordinate date for an initial smoke run (proposed Wed 2027-04-13)
- Redwood (Ben): sanity-check throughput targets and concurrency knobs on our end, ensure streaming concurrency is exercised in harness

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min follow-up if that helps.

Thanks,

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai

Attachment: edgefin_p95_test_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Asha Patel <asha@edgefin.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brandon Liu <brandon.liu@edgefin.ai>, EdgeFin SRE <sre@edgefin.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin — post-demo performance checkpoints (p95/p99)

Thanks, Priyom — this is very helpful. We attached a trimmed production trace (sample_production_trace_202704.zip) and answered the clarifications inline below.

1) Traces: attached include 24h of anonymized request logs with per-request token counts and observed client-side latencies. The trace includes a "cache_hit" flag from our gateway (we think ~55% prefix cache hit historically).
2) TLS: our current setup opens TLS connections from clients; upstream calls reuse HTTP/2 connections to the provider but originate TLS per-client when using mobile clients. For the server-side tests you run, please exercise both "keep-alive" and fresh-TLS scenarios.
3) Short vs Long: roughly 70% short (<= 12 tokens), 20% medium (~64 tokens), 10% long (>=256 tokens) — we'll provide a histogram in the trace file.
4) Routing: we have a single-region egress to the incumbent provider in us-west-2; we can mirror that by running tests from a Redwood region in us-west-2.

Small ask: can Redwood's harness simulate the 2-minute burst pattern? We want to see tail behaviour during bursts. Also, for streaming flows please report token-first-byte and inter-token arrival variance — that matters for perceived responsiveness.

We'll aim to get the production histograms to you by EOD today. Happy to coordinate the smoke run Wed morning PT.

— Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeFin
asha@edgefin.ai

Attachment: sample_production_trace_202704.zip (1.8MB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@edgefin.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Apr 2027 07:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin — post-demo performance checkpoints (p95/p99)

Perfect — thanks for the trace, Asha. Quick notes after a first pass and a proposed lightweight smoke schedule:

Observations from trace:
- Token distribution aligns with your guidance but note our smoke harness will run a slightly higher short-request proportion to stress streaming first-byte latency.
- Cache hit flag present — please confirm if prefix cache is maintained at your edge gateway or in the incumbent provider. That changes warm-up expectations.

Smoke run proposal (Wed 2027-04-13 09:30 PT):
- Duration: 30 minutes warm-up + 30 minutes measurement window
- Steady-state: 120 RPS (mix per trace histogram)
- Bursts: schedule two 2-minute ramps to 420 RPS at minutes 20 and 40
- Streaming: 60% of connections use streaming; streaming concurrency set to 2 streams per client in the harness; measure token-first-byte and final-byte latencies

Measurement outputs we'll share post-run:
- p50/p95/p99 client-observed end-to-end (keep-alive vs fresh-TLS)
- token-first-byte distribution and inter-token interval variance for streaming flows
- request breakdown by token-length buckets and cache-hit vs miss behavior
- raw logs + summarized CSVs uploaded to the Drive link in the related_links field

Ben: can you confirm the host-side config we should use (batching window, KV-cache warmup duration) and whether we should pin a quantized weight profile for parity with the incumbent?

If all good I'll lock Wed 09:30 PT and share the run dashboard link.

Thanks,
— Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@edgefin.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: EdgeFin — post-demo performance checkpoints (p95/p99)

Quick confirmation:
- Batching: we'll run with a conservative dynamic batching window (2–3ms target) for the smoke so we don't over-optimize, and capture per-batch size histograms.
- KV/prefix cache: we'll hold a 12-minute warm-up phase and then mark cache-warm in the harness; this approximates your 55% historical hit rate but we'll instrument hit-rate per-bucket.
- Quantization: we'll test with your incumbent parity profile (int8) and also a midline int8+fp16 hybrid. I'll attach the config snippet to the Drive folder.
- TLS: harness will run both keep-alive and fresh-TLS passes — expect slightly higher p99 on fresh-TLS runs.

One more ask for EdgeFin SREs: please flag any downstream rate-limiting windows (e.g., per-min token caps) so we can throttle the harness if needed.

Ben
Ben Carter
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Asha Patel <asha@edgefin.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brandon Liu <brandon.liu@edgefin.ai>, EdgeFin SRE <sre@edgefin.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin — post-demo performance checkpoints (p95/p99)

Thanks — schedule looks good and we confirmed there's no additional rate-limiting beyond what’s in the trace. SRE will be on-standby for the smoke run. We'll upload the histogram and a short readme about the cache placement to your Drive link in the morning.

See you at 09:30 PT.

— Asha
